newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Varig launches new corporate image.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Varig launches new corporate image.

text.p: Brazil's national airline Varig is spending around $31 million dollars over the next two years to revamp its corporate image in an effort to return to profitability, senior company officials said.
The company posted a first-half loss of 150 million reais ($150 million) this year.

Varig President Fernando Pinto said the company's performance was expected to improve in the second half of 1996, but he declined to comment on whether or not the company expected to post a full-year loss or profit.
"We are looking for an increase in revenues. We aim to achieve a turnover of $3.2 billion (this year)," he said.
"With regard to our annual results we cannot yet make any forecasts. We expect an improvement."
He said sales of $3.2 billion represented an increase of three percent on 1995 turnover.
Varig is spending $16 million to redesign the interior of its aircraft and increase passenger capacity, improve its service on board and on the ground and increase the punctuality of its flights.

Around $15 million will go towards repainting the airlines fleet of 81 aircraft in new yellow and dark blue colors with the company's restyled "rose of the winds" logo. Of the 81 aircraft, two new MD-11 and two new Boeing 727-200 aircraft are to be leased by Varig by April.
The new interior design is due to be finished by July next year, while repainting of all the fuselages will take two years to complete. Varig will also introduce new uniforms in January.
"We needed to transmit the image of a modern company," Pinto said. "We needed to show a company with much enthusiasm and much strength."
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
